proof: Dispatch identity includes tenant and decision identity, so duplicate approval and worker triggers reuse one outbox record.
Two API replicas racing on one tenant/target admit exactly one active decision; the same target remains independently admissible for another tenant.
Concurrent replay attempts against one DLQ record both observe the same durable cooldown and cannot revive it.
Missing or unapproved baseline values produce explicit incomplete input coverage and no fabricated threshold candidate.

Empty, missing, malformed, and all-disabled threshold configuration produces a configuration diagnostic, marks every otherwise-eligible artifact incomplete, and keeps assess_input_coverage, run_tick, and GET /api/evolution/input-coverage fail-closed.
Unsupported execution planes are durably dead-lettered with a reason and leave the EvolutionDecision approved with no execution result.

A direct execute call that re-reads a terminal failed receipt leaves the decision approved, records compensation first, and compare-and-settles the same dispatch intent to the DLQ; duplicate calls cannot add an attempt or obligation.
Production persistence posture refuses the JSON backend before application boot.
Scheduler and threshold worker health stays unready before the first tick, becomes degraded on tick errors, and fails when stale.
Approval prepares and activates a durable tenant-scoped outbox intent before any downstream submit.
The real Research Orchestrator run carries tenant_id and decision_id, and Evolution independently re-reads the run by its immutable downstream reference.
Evolution executes only after terminal completed readback; queued work remains approved and unexecuted.
A crash after approval but before outbox activation is recovered by a fresh dispatch worker process.
Two API processes and restarted workers share one decision/outbox authority and preserve attempt, DLQ, and replay state.
Compose binds API and dispatcher to the same named volume/backend settings and gives all four Evolution processes health or readiness plus a 30-second stop grace period.

A terminal Research failure through either the worker or direct execute API leaves the decision approved, dead-letters the outbox, and records one durable compensation obligation with the real Research run reference.
The compensation ledger survives reconstruction from disk and duplicate failure handling does not create a second obligation.
Evolution never writes RuntimeBinding or downstream governance/deployment state directly.
